source.title: Nine Emotion Centroids: A Label-Free Valence Axis That Transfers Across Four Modalities

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-modal transfer and partial alignment with task-specific valence projections and calibrated CKA, rather than measuring convergence in representational distances as models scale.
record.gate_note: The paper measures cross-modal transfer of a sentiment classifier operating on separately constructed modality-specific axes, and CKA between text, image and audio V-axis projections. It does not test scale- or capability-linked convergence, paired image-caption alignment, seed convergence, or universal features. Individual-modality probe results and causal ablation do not by themselves measure cross-model alignment. Steering and cited results are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Only the calibrated CKA between valence-axis projections (R18–R20) measures cross-encoder alignment directly. It finds alignment small but above a matched-norm null. The 4×4 transfer matrix does not measure mapping between models. Each modality's axis is fitted separately, and a 2-parameter monotone head on a 1-D score cannot change AUC. The off-diagonal columns are identical whatever the source (0.961, 0.764, 0.828, 0.725), so they reflect each target axis's own probe quality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly accurate. Add that the authors present the 4×4 matrix as extending the Platonic Representation Hypothesis to a single task-relevant direction. They also claim the four encoders share no pretraining, though CLIP-text and CLIP-image are jointly trained. They scope 'universal' to the four tested encoders.
record.recipe_differences: Uses emotion-centroid PC1 axes (and a supervised EEG LDA axis), then tests cross-modal sentiment-head transfer and calibrated CKA. It does not reproduce the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis scale-based distance-similarity method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on modality and axis construction: the EEG axis is supervised, while the text, image and audio axes are described as label-free. For Qwen3-8B, sentiment AUC is at chance at mid-depth and peaks at block 31; the paper also reports only family-specific steering. These are not direct tests of convergence sensitivity to similarity metric or input distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: A text-trained 2-parameter head on per-modality valence-axis scores reaches AUC 0.725–0.961 on other modalities. Values are identical across source modalities, so they reflect each modality's separately fitted axis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A continuous attribute (valence) is linearly recoverable, by the same centroid-PC1 recipe, in independently trained encoders of different modalities.

fits_no_version.finding: A generic task-agnostic K=16 shared subspace between encoders gives chance-level sentiment transfer. Raw CLIP-text features give 0.771.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: What a cross-encoder shared subspace captures (object identity) may exclude affective attributes.

record.code_released: not stated (the checklist says code will be released in a camera-ready version; URL omitted)
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 is stated in the paper header; the supplied venue metadata is arXiv.org
record.problems: The alignment evidence is limited to task-specific V-axis projections and a small number of modality pairs. The transfer matrix uses modality-specific axes rather than mapping raw representations; the EEG axis is supervised. CKA is reported as small-magnitude with only a p-value bound, not pair-specific magnitudes. No scale sweep or general representation-distance test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Did not extract individual-modality probe AUCs, the EEG unsupervised-PC1 versus supervised-LDA comparison, depth sweeps, causal ablations, steering results, or categorical-concept failures: these do not directly measure cross-model alignment or mapping for the versions tested here. No results were omitted from the cross-modal transfer matrix, Table 4 bridge comparison, or three reported CKA pairs.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no comparison of general representations across models.
Text↔image CKA is on 1-D valence projections only. There is no image-caption paired alignment and no link between alignment and model quality.
No mapping between representations is fitted or evaluated. The 'transfer' head acts on separately fitted per-modality 1-D axes, and its AUC depends only on the target axis.
No recurring neurons, SAE features or circuits across models.
No comparison of similarity measures, settings or input distributions.
No test of whether shared data or objectives cause the alignment, and no plateau test with scale.

missing.what: Pair-specific CKA magnitudes, and whether any EEG pair was tested (only 3 text/image/audio pairs are reported)

record.verdict_notes: I removed the reader's V4 verdicts. With the sign fixed, a monotone 2-parameter head on a 1-D score cannot change AUC, and Table 3's off-diagonal columns are constant across sources. So the transfer matrix measures per-target probe quality, not interchangeability. The CKA evidence is thin: there are no magnitudes, and how inputs are paired across modalities for CKA is unclear.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep of independently trained models, and no general comparison of their distances on the same inputs.
No alignment test on paired images and captions, or relation between both models' quality and alignment.
No comparison across random initializations of the same architecture.
Tests transfer of a two-parameter classifier between modality-specific valence projections, not general representation mapping, layer stitching, unpaired mapping, or loss under a representation map.
No recurring neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified across models.
No systematic comparison of similarity measures, neighbour settings, or in-/out-of-distribution inputs for the convergence claim.
Reports partial CKA alignment and task-specific shared-subspace comparisons, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause alignment, or whether alignment plateaus with scale.

rows.subject: CLIP-image-768
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated a text-trained logistic-regression head on image V-axis projections
rows.note: The head was fitted on source-modality labels; no target-modality labels were used at head-fitting.
rows.check: Text→image AUC 0.961 equals the image column for every source, so the head is irrelevant. This is image-axis probe quality, not a representation mapping. The baseline should be the random-direction 0.52–0.59 (Table 3 caption).

rows.subject: CLAP-audio-512
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated a text-trained logistic-regression head on audio V-axis projections
rows.note: No target-modality labels were used at head-fitting.
rows.check: 0.764 is identical for all sources, so it measures the audio axis alone, not cross-model mapping. Baseline: random 0.52–0.59.

rows.subject: CBraMod-200
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated a text-trained logistic-regression head on EEG V-axis projections
rows.note: The EEG axis itself was fitted using FACED binary-valence labels; the classifier head used no EEG labels.
rows.check: 0.828 is identical for all sources. The EEG axis is a supervised LDA, so the value is EEG probe quality, not alignment. Baseline: random 0.52–0.59.

rows.subject: CLIP-text and CLIP-image
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated text-to-image sentiment transfer using a generic shared substrate
rows.note: Generic shared-subspace baseline did not transfer sentiment effectively.
rows.check: It is not stated how a text-trained classifier is applied through the 'generic K=16 substrate'. The substrate is within the jointly trained CLIP family. It shows a task-agnostic subspace lacks sentiment, not the degree of convergence.

rows.subject: CLIP-text and CLIP-image
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated text-to-image sentiment transfer using a random subspace
rows.note: The text reports approximately chance performance, without a more precise value.
rows.check: A random-subspace control for the study's own method comparison; it is not a convergence measure.

rows.subject: CLIP-text and CLAP-audio
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated text-to-image sentiment transfer using a cross-encoder-family substrate
rows.note: The text reports approximately chance performance, without a more precise value.
rows.check: The bridge is a CLIP-text+CLAP-audio substrate, yet the result is evaluated text→image. The method is underspecified and the value is only '≈ chance'.

rows.subject: CLIP-text
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated text-to-image sentiment transfer using raw text-encoder features
rows.note: Transfer occurs, but the reported AUC is below the V-axis result.
rows.check: Raw CLIP-text features transferring to CLIP-image reflects CLIP's joint contrastive embedding space, not convergence of independent models. This is a method comparison.

rows.subject: CLIP-text and CLIP-image
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated text-to-image sentiment transfer using the V-axis bridge
rows.note: This is the same text-to-image value also reported in Table 3.
rows.check: Same value as R1, used as the study's own method in the bridge comparison; it is redundant.

rows.subject: CLIP-text and CLIP-image
rows.operation_detail: Measured Pang-calibrated CKA between V-axis projections
rows.measure: CKA alignment; authors describe magnitude as small but reliably above chance
rows.note: The paper gives a significance bound for all three reported pairs, not a pair-specific CKA magnitude.
rows.check: CKA rejects the null (p≤0.032) but no magnitude is given; the authors call it small. The input pairing across modalities is unstated. CLIP-text and CLIP-image are jointly trained, so shared training could explain the alignment.

rows.measure: CKA alignment; authors describe magnitude as small but reliably above chance
rows.note: The paper gives a significance bound for all three reported pairs, not a pair-specific CKA magnitude.
rows.check: Small-magnitude CKA above null, with no magnitude. Pairing of inputs is unstated. CLAP is text-audio contrastive, so it shares an objective with the text side.

rows.subject: CLIP-image and CLAP-audio
rows.operation_detail: Measured Pang-calibrated CKA between V-axis projections
rows.measure: CKA alignment; authors describe magnitude as small but reliably above chance
rows.note: The paper gives a significance bound for all three reported pairs, not a pair-specific CKA magnitude.
rows.check: Small-magnitude CKA above null, with no magnitude and pairing unstated.

relationships.condition: Calibrated CKA between valence-axis projections of CLIP-text, CLIP-image and CLAP-audio
relationships.reason: All three pairs are above the matched-norm null (p≤0.032) but described as small-magnitude, so alignment is partial (R18–R20). The construct is narrow and no magnitudes are given.
relationships.display_finding: All three modality pairs exceeded the matched-norm null at p ≤ 0.032, but the authors described their alignment as small.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: All 12 off-diagonal modality transfers in the four-modality V-axis matrix
reader_labels.reason: Every reported cross-modal head transfer has AUC at least 0.70; the separate V-axis text-to-image result is 0.961 (R1–R12, R17). This supports transfer of the task-specific classifier, not general interchangeability of raw representations.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Text-to-image transfer using generic shared or raw-feature bridges
reader_labels.reason: Generic K=16 and random-subspace bridges are at or near chance, while raw CLIP-text features reach 0.771 rather than the V-axis bridge's 0.961; transfer depends on the task-specific valence axis (R13–R16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Text-image-audio V-axis pairs and generic shared-subspace sentiment transfer
reader_labels.reason: CKA is statistically above the matched-norm null but described as small in magnitude, and a generic K=16 substrate is at 0.525 AUC for sentiment transfer; the findings indicate partial, task-dependent alignment rather than complete general agreement (R13, R18–R20).
